Population-level physical activity programs have demonstrated cost-effectiveness in multiple national healthcare systems by generating net savings through reduced disease burden and improved productivity. Large-scale initiatives in countries such as the United Kingdom, Australia, and Finland have tracked participants over multi-year periods and documented lower per-capita medical expenditures, fewer workdays lost to illness, and decreased utilization of specialist services, confirming that modest public investments in exercise infrastructure and community programs yield sustained fiscal returns at the societal level.
